title: Undersea internet cables: the internet lives on the ocean floor
description:
Over 99% of intercontinental internet traffic doesn't go through satellites. It runs through undersea cables almost 1.5 million km long in total. Find out how thick these cables are, what threatens them, and when the first one was laid.
#shorts #tech #internet #oceanfacts

scenes.narration: The internet between continents sits on the ocean floor. Literally.
scenes.imagePrompt: thick fiber optic cable lying on the dark ocean floor, faint light pulses inside it, deep blue haze, deep midnight blue palette with cyan highlights, cinematic lighting, shallow depth of field, no text

scenes.narration: You'd think data flies through satellites. But satellites carry only a tiny slice of the world's traffic.
scenes.imagePrompt: communication satellite orbiting earth at night, small and distant, deep midnight blue palette with cyan highlights, cinematic lighting, shallow depth of field, no text

scenes.narration: More than ninety-nine percent of data between continents travels through undersea cables. And there are hundreds of them.

stat.label: of intercontinental traffic goes by cable

scenes.imagePrompt: glowing world map with bright lines of cables crossing the oceans, deep midnight blue palette with cyan highlights, cinematic lighting, shallow depth of field, no text

scenes.narration: Together they stretch almost one and a half million kilometers. That's enough to reach the Moon more than three times.
scenes.imagePrompt: a thin glowing line stretching from earth toward the moon in space, deep midnight blue palette with cyan highlights, cinematic lighting, shallow depth of field, no text

scenes.narration: Yet a deep-sea cable is about as thick as a garden hose. Inside are thin glass fibers carrying pulses of light.
scenes.imagePrompt: cross-section of a submarine cable with glowing glass fibers in the center, macro, deep midnight blue palette with cyan highlights, cinematic lighting, shallow depth of field, no text

scenes.narration: Their biggest threat isn't sharks. It's ship anchors and fishing trawlers. Special ships go out to repair them.
scenes.imagePrompt: heavy ship anchor and chain sinking through murky water, deep midnight blue palette with cyan highlights, cinematic lighting, shallow depth of field, no text

scenes.narration: The first cable across the Atlantic was laid way back in eighteen fifty-eight. It carried telegrams and lasted less than a month.
scenes.imagePrompt: antique telegraph key and coiled cable on a wooden desk, 19th century atmosphere, deep midnight blue palette with cyan highlights, cinematic lighting, shallow depth of field, no text

scenes.narration: Did you know the internet lies on the ocean floor? Tell me in the comments.
